        res=run(name)
        ok = "OK" if res=="OK" else "FAIL"

import pty, os, subprocess, time, select

# Try running executable under pty with fake ping
import os
env = dict(os.environ)
env["PATH"] = "/tmp/fakebin:" + env["PATH"]

# Use script to capture? Let's use python pty
def run_pty(args, timeout=4):
    # create pty pair
    import pty, subprocess, os, select, time
    master, slave = pty.openpty()
    # set winsize? default 80x24
    p = subprocess.Popen(
        ["./executable"]+args,
        stdin=slave, stdout=slave, stderr=slave,
        env=env,
        close_fds=True,
    )
    os.close(slave)
    # nonblocking read
    import fcntl
    flags = fcntl.fcntl(master, fcntl.F_GETFL)
    fcntl.fcntl(master, fcntl.F_SETFL, flags | os.O_NONBLOCK)
    output = b""
    start = time.time()
    while time.time()-start < timeout:
        try:
            r,_,_ = select.select([master], [], [], 0.5)
            if r:
                try:
                    data = os.read(master, 4096)
                    if not data:
                        break
                    output += data
                except OSError:
                    break
        except Exception as e:
            print(e)
            break
        if p.poll() is not None:
            # process exited, drain
            try:
                while True:
                    data = os.read(master, 4096)
                    if not data: break
                    output+=data
            except: pass
            break
    # kill
    try: p.terminate()
    except: pass
    try: p.wait(timeout=1)
    except: p.kill()
    os.close(master)
    return p.returncode, output

for args in [["127.0.0.1"], ["--cmd","echo hi"]]:

    except Exception as e: print(e)
    print("==============")

    open("/tmp/ping.log","w").write("")
    env = dict(os.environ)
    env["PATH"] = "/tmp/fakebin:" + env["PATH"]
    # run under pty briefly to capture ping invocation, then kill
    import pty, fcntl, termios, struct, select
    master, slave = pty.openpty()
    fcntl.ioctl(slave, termios.TIOCSWINSZ, struct.pack("HHHH", 24, 80, 0, 0))
    p = subprocess.Popen(["./executable"]+extra_args, stdin=slave, stdout=slave, stderr=slave, env=env)
    import os as _os
    _os.close(slave)
    time.sleep(1.5)
    try: p.terminate()
    except: pass
    try: p.wait(timeout=1)
    except: p.kill()
    _os.close(master)
    log = open("/tmp/ping.log").read().strip().split("\n")
    return log

    (["127.0.0.1"], "default"),
    (["-n","0.5","127.0.0.1"], "interval 0.5"),
    (["-4","127.0.0.1"], "ipv4"),
    (["-6","::1"], "ipv6"),
    (["-i","eth0","127.0.0.1"], "interface"),
    (["127.0.0.1","--ping-args","-c","1"], "ping-args -c 1"),

    (["localhost"], "localhost"),

messages.content: 0 # gping 🚀 [![Crates.io](https://img.shields.io/crates/v/gping.svg)](https://crates.io/crates/gping) [![Actions Status](https://github.com/orf/gping/workflows/CI/badge.svg)](https://github.com/orf/gping/actions) Ping, but with a graph. ![](./images/readme-example.gif) Comes with the following super-powers: * Graph the ping time for multiple hosts * Graph the _execution time_ for commands via the `--cmd` flag * Custom colours * Windows, Mac and Linux support Table of Contents ================= * [Install :cd:](#install-cd) * [Usage :saxophone:](#usage-saxophone) # Install :cd: * macOS * [Homebrew](https://formulae.brew.sh/formula/gping#default): `brew install gping` * [MacPorts](https://ports.macports.org/port/gping/): `sudo port install gping` * Linux (Homebrew): `brew install gping` * CentOS (and other distributions with an old glibc): Download the MUSL build from the latest release * Windows/ARM: * Scoop: `scoop install gping` * Chocolatey: `choco install gping` * Download the latest release from [the github releases page](https://github.com/orf/gping/releases) * Fedora ([COPR](https://copr.fedorainfracloud.org/coprs/atim/gping/)): `sudo dnf copr enable atim/gping -y && sudo dnf install gping` * Cargo (**This requires `rustc` version 1.67.0 or greater**): `cargo install gping` * Arch Linux: `pacman -S gping` * Alpine linux: `apk add gping` * Ubuntu >23.10/Debian >13: `apt install gping` * Ubuntu/Debian ([Azlux's repo](https://packages.azlux.fr/)): ```bash echo 'deb [signed-by=/usr/share/keyrings/azlux.gpg] https://packages.azlux.fr/debian/ bookworm main' | sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/azlux.list sudo apt install gpg curl -s https://azlux.fr/repo.gpg.key | gpg --dearmor | sudo tee /usr/share/keyrings/azlux.gpg > /dev/null sudo apt update sudo apt install gping ``` * Gentoo ([dm9pZCAq overlay](https://github.com/gentoo-mirror/dm9pZCAq)): ```sh sudo eselect repository enable dm9pZCAq sudo emerge --sync dm9pZCAq sudo emerge net-misc/gping::dm9pZCAq ``` * FreeBSD: * [pkg](https://www.freshports.org/net-mgmt/gping/): `pkg install gping` * [ports](https://cgit.freebsd.org/ports/tree/net-mgmt/gping) `cd /usr/ports/net-mgmt/gping; make install clean` * Docker: ```sh # Check all options docker run --rm -ti --network host ghcr.io/orf/gping:gping-v1.15.1 --help # Ping google.com docker run --rm -ti --network host ghcr.io/orf/gping:gping-v1.15.1 google.com ``` * Flox: ```sh # Inside of a Flox environment flox install gping ``` * [gah](https://github.com/marverix/gah): ```sh gah install gping ``` # Usage :saxophone: Just run `gping [host]`. `host` can be a command like `curl google.com` if the `--cmd` flag is used. You can also use shorthands like `aws:eu-west-1` or `aws:ca-central-1` to ping specific cloud regions. Only `aws` is currently supported. ```bash $ gping --help Ping, but with a graph. Usage: gping [OPTIONS] [HOSTS_OR_COMMANDS]... Arguments: [HOSTS_OR_COMMANDS]... Hosts or IPs to ping, or commands to run if --cmd is provided. Can use cloud shorthands like aws:eu-west-1. Options: --cmd Graph the execution time for a list of commands rather than pinging hosts -n, --watch-interval Watch interval seconds (provide partial seconds like '0.5'). Default for ping is 0.2, default for cmd is 0.5. -b, --buffer Determines the number of seconds to display in the graph. [default: 30] -4 Resolve ping targets to IPv4 address -6 Resolve ping targets to IPv6 address -i, --interface Interface to use when pinging -s, --simple-graphics Uses dot characters instead of braille --vertical-margin Vertical margin around the graph (top and bottom) [default: 1] --horizontal-margin Horizontal margin around the graph (left and right) [default: 0] -c, --color Assign color to a graph entry. This option can be defined more than once as a comma separated string, and the order which the colors are provided will be matched against the hosts or commands passed to gping. Hexadecimal RGB color codes are accepted in the form of '#RRGGBB' or the following color names: 'black', 'red', 'green', 'yellow', 'blue', 'magenta','cyan', 'gray', 'dark-gray', 'light-red', 'light-green', 'light-yellow', 'light-blue', 'light-magenta', 'light-cyan', and 'white' -h, --help Print help information -V, --version Print version information --clear Clear the graph from the terminal after closing the program ``` ====== .ie \n(.g .ds Aq \(aq .el .ds Aq ' .TH gping 1 "gping " .SH NAME gping \- Ping, but with a graph. .SH SYNOPSIS \fBgping\fR [\fB\-\-cmd\fR] [\fB\-n\fR|\fB\-\-watch\-interval\fR] [\fB\-b\fR|\fB\-\-buffer\fR] [\fB\-4 \fR] [\fB\-6 \fR] [\fB\-i\fR|\fB\-\-interface\fR] [\fB\-s\fR|\fB\-\-simple\-graphics\fR] [\fB\-\-vertical\-margin\fR] [\fB\-\-horizontal\-margin\fR] [\fB\-c\fR|\fB\-\-color\fR] [\fB\-\-clear\fR] [\fB\-\-ping\-args\fR] [\fB\-h\fR|\fB\-\-help\fR] [\fIHOSTS_OR_COMMANDS\fR] .SH DESCRIPTION Ping, but with a graph. .SH OPTIONS .TP \fB\-\-cmd\fR Graph the execution time for a list of commands rather than pinging hosts .TP \fB\-n\fR, \fB\-\-watch\-interval\fR \fI\fR Watch interval seconds (provide partial seconds like \*(Aq0.5\*(Aq). Default for ping is 0.2, default for cmd is 0.5 .TP \fB\-b\fR, \fB\-\-buffer\fR \fI\fR [default: 30] Determines the number of seconds to display in the graph .TP \fB\-4\fR Resolve ping targets to IPv4 address .TP \fB\-6\fR Resolve ping targets to IPv6 address .TP \fB\-i\fR, \fB\-\-interface\fR \fI\fR Interface to use when pinging .TP \fB\-s\fR, \fB\-\-simple\-graphics\fR .TP \fB\-\-vertical\-margin\fR \fI\fR [default: 1] Vertical margin around the graph (top and bottom) .TP \fB\-\-horizontal\-margin\fR \fI\fR [default: 0] Horizontal margin around the graph (left and right) .TP \fB\-c\fR, \fB\-\-color\fR \fI\fR Assign color to a graph entry. This option can be defined more than once as a comma separated string, and the order which the colors are provided will be matched against the hosts or commands passed to gping. Hexadecimal RGB color codes are accepted in the form of \*(Aq#RRGGBB\*(Aq or the following color names: \*(Aqblack\*(Aq, \*(Aqred\*(Aq, \*(Aqgreen\*(Aq, \*(Aqyellow\*(Aq, \*(Aqblue\*(Aq, \*(Aqmagenta\*(Aq, \*(Aqcyan\*(Aq, \*(Aqgray\*(Aq, \*(Aqdark\-gray\*(Aq, \*(Aqlight\-red\*(Aq, \*(Aqlight\-green\*(Aq, \*(Aqlight\-yellow\*(Aq, \*(Aqlight\-blue\*(Aq, \*(Aqlight\-magenta\*(Aq, \*(Aqlight\-cyan\*(Aq, and \*(Aqwhite\*(Aq .TP \fB\-\-clear\fR Clear the graph from the terminal after closing the program .TP \fB\-\-ping\-args\fR [\fI...\fR] Extra arguments to pass to `ping`. These are platform dependent .TP \fB\-h\fR, \fB\-\-help\fR Print help .TP [\fIHOSTS_OR_COMMANDS\fR] Hosts or IPs to ping, or commands to run if \-\-cmd is provided. ]:

        .arg(Arg::new("cmd").long("cmd").action(ArgAction::SetTrue).help("Graph the execution time for a list of commands rather than pinging hosts"))
        .arg(Arg::new("watch-interval").short('n').long("watch-interval").value_name("WATCH_INTERVAL").help("Watch interval seconds (provide partial seconds like '0.5'). Default for ping is 0.2, default for cmd is 0.5"))

        .arg(Arg::new("ipv4").short('4').action(ArgAction::SetTrue).conflicts_with("ipv6").help("Resolve ping targets to IPv4 address"))
        .arg(Arg::new("ipv6").short('6').action(ArgAction::SetTrue).conflicts_with("ipv4").help("Resolve ping targets to IPv6 address"))
        .arg(Arg::new("interface").short('i').long("interface").value_name("INTERFACE").help("Interface to use when pinging"))
        .arg(Arg::new("simple-graphics").short('s').long("simple-graphics").action(ArgAction::SetTrue))
        .arg(Arg::new("vertical-margin").long("vertical-margin").value_name("VERTICAL_MARGIN").default_value("1").help("Vertical margin around the graph (top and bottom)"))
        .arg(Arg::new("horizontal-margin").long("horizontal-margin").value_name("HORIZONTAL_MARGIN").default_value("0").help("Horizontal margin around the graph (left and right)"))
        .arg(Arg::new("color").short('c').long("color").value_name("color").help("Assign color to a graph entry.\n\nThis option can be defined more than once as a comma separated string, and the order which the colors are provided will be matched against the hosts or commands passed to gping.\n\nHexadecimal RGB color codes are accepted in the form of '#RRGGBB' or the following color names: 'black', 'red', 'green', 'yellow', 'blue', 'magenta', 'cyan', 'gray', 'dark-gray', 'light-red', 'light-green', 'light-yellow', 'light-blue', 'light-magenta', 'light-cyan', and 'white'"))
        .arg(Arg::new("clear").long("clear").action(ArgAction::SetTrue).help("Clear the graph from the terminal after closing the program"))
        .arg(Arg::new("ping-args").long("ping-args").value_name("PING_ARGS").num_args(0..).allow_hyphen_values(true).help("Extra arguments to pass to `ping`. These are platform dependent"))
        .arg(Arg::new("HOSTS_OR_COMMANDS").value_name("HOSTS_OR_COMMANDS").num_args(0..).help("Hosts or IPs to ping, or commands to run if --cmd is provided. Can use cloud shorthands like aws:eu-west-1"))
}
fn main() {

    println!("ping={:?} hosts={:?}", ping, hosts);
}

impl FromStr for Color {
    type Err = ParseColorError;

    fn from_str(s: &str) -> Result<Self, Self::Err> {
        Ok(
            // There is a mix of different color names and formats in the wild.
            // This is an attempt to support as many as possible.
            match s
                .to_lowercase()
                .replace([' ', '-', '_'], "")
                .replace("bright", "light")
                .replace("grey", "gray")
                .replace("silver", "gray")
                .replace("lightblack", "darkgray")
                .replace("lightwhite", "white")
                .replace("lightgray", "white")
                .as_ref()
            {
                "reset" => Self::Reset,
                "black" => Self::Black,
                "red" => Self::Red,
                "green" => Self::Green,
                "yellow" => Self::Yellow,
                "blue" => Self::Blue,
                "magenta" => Self::Magenta,
                "cyan" => Self::Cyan,
                "gray" => Self::Gray,
                "darkgray" => Self::DarkGray,
                "lightred" => Self::LightRed,
                "lightgreen" => Self::LightGreen,
                "lightyellow" => Self::LightYellow,
                "lightblue" => Self::LightBlue,
                "lightmagenta" => Self::LightMagenta,
                "lightcyan" => Self::LightCyan,
                "white" => Self::White,
                _ => {
                    if let Ok(index) = s.parse::<u8>() {
                        Self::Indexed(index)
                    } else if let Some((r, g, b)) = parse_hex_color(s) {
                        Self::Rgb(r, g, b)
                    } else {
                        return Err(ParseColorError);
                    }
                }
            },
        )
    }
}

fn parse_hex_color(input: &str) -> Option<(u8, u8, u8)> {
    if !input.starts_with('#') || input.len() != 7 {
        return None;
    }
    let r = u8::from_str_radix(input.get(1..3)?, 16).ok()?;
    let g = u8::from_str_radix(input.get(3..5)?, 16).ok()?;
    let b = u8::from_str_radix(input.get(5..7)?, 16).ok()?;
    Some((r, g, b))
}

use clap::{Arg, ArgAction, Command, value_parser};
use anyhow::{Context, anyhow};

fn build_cli() -> Command {
    Command::new("gping")
        .version("1.20.1")
        .long_version("gping 1.20.1\ncommit_hash: 42449c03\nbuild_time: 2026-08-10 23:10:43 +00:00\nbuild_env: rustc 1.92.0 (ded5c06cf 2025-12-08),1.92.0-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu")
        .about("Ping, but with a graph.")
        .arg(Arg::new("cmd").long("cmd").action(ArgAction::SetTrue).conflicts_with("ping-args").help("Graph the execution time for a list of commands rather than pinging hosts"))
        .arg(Arg::new("watch-interval").short('n').long("watch-interval").value_name("WATCH_INTERVAL").value_parser(value_parser!(f32)).help("Watch interval seconds (provide partial seconds like '0.5'). Default for ping is 0.2, default for cmd is 0.5"))
        .arg(Arg::new("buffer").short('b').long("buffer").value_name("BUFFER").value_parser(value_parser!(u64)).default_value("30").help("Determines the number of seconds to display in the graph"))
        .arg(Arg::new("ipv4").short('4').action(ArgAction::SetTrue).conflicts_with("ipv6").help("Resolve ping targets to IPv4 address"))
        .arg(Arg::new("ipv6").short('6').action(ArgAction::SetTrue).conflicts_with("ipv4").help("Resolve ping targets to IPv6 address"))
        .arg(Arg::new("interface").short('i').long("interface").value_name("INTERFACE").help("Interface to use when pinging"))
        .arg(Arg::new("simple-graphics").short('s').long("simple-graphics").action(ArgAction::SetTrue))
        .arg(Arg::new("vertical-margin").long("vertical-margin").value_name("VERTICAL_MARGIN").value_parser(value_parser!(u16)).default_value("1").help("Vertical margin around the graph (top and bottom)"))
        .arg(Arg::new("horizontal-margin").long("horizontal-margin").value_name("HORIZONTAL_MARGIN").value_parser(value_parser!(u16)).default_value("0").help("Horizontal margin around the graph (left and right)"))
        .arg(Arg::new("color").short('c').long("color").value_name("color").action(ArgAction::Append).help("Assign color to a graph entry.\n\nThis option can be defined more than once as a comma separated string, and the order which the colors are provided will be matched against the hosts or commands passed to gping.\n\nHexadecimal RGB color codes are accepted in the form of '#RRGGBB' or the following color names: 'black', 'red', 'green', 'yellow', 'blue', 'magenta', 'cyan', 'gray', 'dark-gray', 'light-red', 'light-green', 'light-yellow', 'light-blue', 'light-magenta', 'light-cyan', and 'white'"))
        .arg(Arg::new("clear").long("clear").action(ArgAction::SetTrue).help("Clear the graph from the terminal after closing the program"))
        .arg(Arg::new("ping-args").long("ping-args").value_name("PING_ARGS").num_args(0..).allow_hyphen_values(true).action(ArgAction::Append).help("Extra arguments to pass to `ping`. These are platform dependent"))
        .arg(Arg::new("HOSTS_OR_COMMANDS").value_name("HOSTS_OR_COMMANDS").num_args(0..).help("Hosts or IPs to ping, or commands to run if --cmd is provided. Can use cloud shorthands like aws:eu-west-1"))
}

fn main() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
    // manual handling for --ping-args trailing (space form consumes all remaining)

p = pathlib.Path("src/main.rs").read_text()
# fix color: swap outer/inner

# Wait: anyhow!("Failed").context("Invalid") gives outer Invalid, inner Failed? Actually context adds outer. So anyhow!("Failed").context("Invalid") => outer Invalid, inner Failed. Good.
# But our new is anyhow!("Failed").context(format!("Invalid...")) => outer Invalid, inner Failed. Good.
# However, the original error's Display for outer is "Invalid...", inner "Failed...". That's what we want.

# Our old was anyhow!("Invalid").context("Failed") => "Failed\n\nCaused by:\n    Invalid" (wrong).
# So fix.
assert old in p
p = p.replace(old, new)
# fix spawning: currently anyhow!("Error spawning ping: {}", e).context(e.to_string())
# This gives outer e.to_string() ("No such..."), inner "Error spawning ping: ..." (wrong order). Need outer "Error spawning...", inner e.to_string().
# So swap: anyhow!(e.to_string()).context(format!("Error spawning ping: {}", e))
old2 = 'anyhow!("Error spawning ping: {}", e).context(e.to_string())'
new2 = 'anyhow!(e.to_string()).context(format!("Error spawning ping: {}", e))'
# There are two occurrences (for -V and for actual ping). Replace both.
assert p.count(old2) == 2
p = p.replace(old2, new2)
pathlib.Path("src/main.rs").write_text(p)
print("fixed")

import subprocess, os, time, pty, fcntl, termios, struct, select
def capture(args, rows=24, cols=120, timeout=4):
    env=dict(os.environ); env["PATH"]="/tmp/fakebin:"+env["PATH"]; env["TERM"]="xterm-256color"
    master, slave = pty.openpty()
    fcntl.ioctl(slave, termios.TIOCSWINSZ, struct.pack("HHHH", rows,cols,0,0))
    p=subprocess.Popen(["./executable"]+args, stdin=slave, stdout=slave, stderr=slave, env=env)
    import os as _os; _os.close(slave)
    flags=fcntl.fcntl(master, fcntl.F_GETFL)
    fcntl.fcntl(master, fcntl.F_SETFL, flags|_os.O_NONBLOCK)
    out=b""
    start=time.time()
    while time.time()-start<timeout:
        r,_,_=select.select([master],[],[],0.5)
        if r:
            try:
                d=_os.read(master,8192)
                if not d: break
                out+=d
            except: break
        if p.poll() is not None:
            try:
                while True:
                    d=_os.read(master,8192)
                    if not d: break
                    out+=d
            except: pass
            break
    try: p.terminate()
    except: pass
    try: p.wait(timeout=1)
    except: p.kill()
    _os.close(master)
    return out

# test simple graphics

print("simple len",len(out2))
print(repr(out2[:4000].decode(errors="replace")))
